newsitem.title: NORWAY: Japan to upgrade contacts with North Korea.
newsitem.headline: Japan to upgrade contacts with North Korea.

text.p: BERGEN, Norway, June 26 - Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto said on Thursday that Japan planned to upgrade talks with North Korea to tackle allegations that Japanese nationals were kidnapped by North Korean agents in the late 1970s and 1980s, and other bilateral issues.

Hashimoto, visiting Norway for a summit with the leaders of five Nordic countries, told reporters that he mentioned Japan's intention of upgrading the talks with North Korea to South Korean President Kim Young-sam when they met in New York on Monday.
"I told the president that Japan plans to raise a level of governmental contacts with North Korea," he said.
Hashimoto made the remarks when he was asked when Japan would make a decision on food aid to North Korea.

Japanese government officials have said Tokyo's policy on food aid to North Korea depends on the results of current talks over the alleged kidnapping cases and a big drug seizure aboard a North Korean freighter.
Japan currently sends officials from the Foreign Ministry's section in charge of North East Asian affairs, led by the section chief.
"We will now have more senior officials at talks with North Korea...We want to make Japan's position clear and we want a clear reply from North Korea," Hashimoto said.

There has been speculation that Japan will soon make a decision on providing food aid to North Korea as the United States and South Korea are increasing pressure on Tokyo to provide such aid to the famine-threatened country.
In his talks with the South Korean president in New York, Hashimoto suggested that Japan was still cautious about providing aid to North Korea.
"Hashimoto told the president that Japan's position on food aid to North Korea is still severe," a Japanese official said.
